# Test different comparison operators

# Initialize git repo
exec git init
exec git config user.name "Test User"
exec git config user.email "test@example.com"

# Create main branch with 5 files only
exec git checkout -b main
exec git add file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt file4.txt file5.txt
exec git commit -m 'main with 5 files'

# Create feature branch with 7 files (improvement)
exec git checkout -b feature
exec git add file6.txt file7.txt
exec git commit -m 'feature with 7 files'

# Test greater-than (7 > 5) - use git ls-files to count tracked files
exec ratchet --gt main 'git ls-files "*.txt" | wc -l'
stdout 'Success: HEAD metric \(7\) is greater than main \(5\)'

# Test greater-equal (7 >= 5)
exec ratchet --ge main 'git ls-files "*.txt" | wc -l'
stdout 'Success: HEAD metric \(7\) is greater than or equal to main \(5\)'

# Test less-than should fail (7 < 5 is false)
! exec ratchet --lt main 'git ls-files "*.txt" | wc -l'
stderr 'Error: HEAD metric \(7\) is NOT less than main \(5\)'

# Test equal-to should fail (7 == 5 is false)
! exec ratchet --eq main 'git ls-files "*.txt" | wc -l'
stderr 'Error: HEAD metric \(7\) is NOT equal to main \(5\)'

# Switch to main and test equal with itself
exec git checkout main
exec ratchet --eq main 'git ls-files "*.txt" | wc -l'
stdout 'Success: HEAD metric \(5\) is equal to main \(5\)'

content
-- file2.txt --

content

content

content
